html:
The Anglo-Nepalese War was fought from 1814 to 1816 between the East India Company and the Gorkha kingdom of Nepal. Nepal lost a third of its land and kept its independence.

In fifty years the Gorkhas had conquered the Kathmandu valley (see Prithvi Narayan Shah) and then a strip of the Himalayas 1,300 kilometres long, from Sikkim to the Sutlej River. Their push into the plains at its foot met the Company's push north.

The British sent four columns into the hills in 1814. Three failed. At the small fort of Kalanga 600 Gorkhas, with women and children, held off thousands for a month, and the British general was killed. Only David Ochterlony, in the far west, made steady progress by hauling guns up the ridges. In 1816 he turned the passes that guard Kathmandu, and the court gave in.

By the Treaty of Sugauli Nepal gave up Kumaon, Garhwal, Sikkim and much of the lowland strip, and accepted a British resident in Kathmandu. Its present borders date from then.

The British had admired their enemy. They began recruiting Gorkha soldiers during the war itself, and Gurkha regiments have served in the British and Indian armies ever since. Nepal was never colonised.
sum: The Anglo-Nepalese War was fought from 1814 to 1816 between the East India Company and the Gorkha kingdom of Nepal. Nepal lost a third of its land and kept its independence.
